newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Perth power blackout threat eases with return to work.
newsitem.headline: Perth power blackout threat eases with return to work.

text.p: The threat of widespread blackouts in Perth and throughout the south-west corner of Western Australia subsided on Friday after one group of striking power workers returned to work.
A spokesman for Western Power, the utility affected by the industrial action, said 25 coal plant handling operators at the Muja Power Station near Collie turned up for work this afternoon.
"We have just had the word that the operators were walking back in the gate a couple of minutes ago," the spokesman said.

"However, the power restrictions (imposed yesterday under emergency power legislation and applying to all 690,000 customers in the South West Interconnected System) are still in force, until we can crank up the Station.
"They stay on until we are confident we can maintain a constant power supply. That should be sometime late this afternoon."
Another group of 44 power plant operators at the Kwinana Power Station in Perth were meeting to decide whether to end their industrial action, which shut down that station late last week.

The Kwinana dispute originally involved work bans over a staffing level disagreement but escalated into a strike, and spread to Muja, after Western Power told the workers the federal Workplace Relations Act prohibited the utility from paying them while they were taking industrial action.
The workers' union, the Construction, Forestry, Mining and Energy Union, also linked the industrial action to a campaign of protest over proposed changes to WA's industrial relations system.

Yesterday the Australian Industrial Relations Commission ordered an immediate return to work but the CMFEU sought further clarification of the order from the Commission this morning before convening workplace meetings.
